title: Vitamin D and Marine n-3 Fatty Acids for Autoimmune Disease Prevention: Outcomes Two Years After Completion of a Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial
authors: Costenbader KH, Cook NR, Lee IM, Hahn J, Walter J, Bubes V, et al.
followUp: 5.3-year randomised period plus 2 years of observational follow-up in 21,592 participants (83.5%)
population: VITAL participants: US men aged 50 years or older and women aged 55 years or older; history of renal failure or dialysis, cirrhosis, hypercalcaemia, cancer, cardiovascular disease or other serious illness excluded
funder: Supported by the NIH (grants R01-AR-059086, K24-AR-066109, U01-CA-138962, R01-CA-138962 and R01-AT-011729). No statement on the role of the funder was found.
inKindSupport: The vitamin D pill and its matching placebo were prepared by Pharmavite LLC; the n-3 fatty acid pill and its placebo by Pronova BioPharma.
authorConflicts: Author disclosures are available at the publisher's site; not read.
result: With two more years of observation after the trial, confirmed autoimmune disease occurred in 255 participants originally randomised to vitamin D3 2000 IU/day against 259 randomised to its placebo, HR 0.98 (95% CI 0.83 to 1.17) at 7 years. Of newly confirmed cases, 65 had onset during the randomised period; including them changed the randomised-period result for vitamin D to HR 0.85 (0.70 to 1.04). The authors conclude that the protective effects of vitamin D dissipated two years after trial termination; psoriasis was the only disease with a sustained, significant reduction (HR 0.61, 0.38 to 0.98).
